title: Velocity cohort prober and regression bisector for TPS microlab
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a robust, cohort-based tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness (the 'cohort prober') that can: run targeted velocity tests across model variants/quantizations, intelligently morph workload characteristics (seq length, prompt prefix entropy, batch vs single), sweep concurrency, and feed p95/p99 signals into our regression bisector. The goal is to detect subtle TPS regressions early in CI and provide a minimal-action bisector that narrows regressions to a commit, model change, or kernel/quant path within a day.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute >10k steady-state token/s steady probes across 3 model families (Llama2-like, Mistral-like, openLlaMA-like) and report per-cohort p50/p95/p99 and token/sec
Adaptive concurrency sweep produces stable TPS curves and exports the chosen operating point used by Console for SLA verification
Regression bisector can isolate a TPS regression to a single commit within a provided PR range >= 95% of the time on synthetic regressions injected for test
CI job 'tps-cohort-prober' runs in < 45 minutes and fails a build when p95 degrades by configured delta (default 8%) vs golden baseline
Dashboard panel shows cohort breakdowns (quant, seq_len, prompt-shape) and links to bisector runs and suspected commits
technical_notes: Use existing microbench harness as base but add a workload morphing layer to vary token distributions and deterministic prompt seeding
Bisector algorithm: hierarchical binary bisect (commit-range -> model-variant -> kernel-path) with lightweight replay harness to reproduce TPS deltas
Metric collection: push aggregated histograms (p50/p95/p99) and sample-level latencies to Prometheus + long-term metrics store for drift detection
Cost control: runtime should run on preemptible nodes with a token cap per run and early-abort when 95% CI for p95 is stable

test_plan: Unit tests for workload morphing and deterministic prompt seeding
Integration test: run 3 cohort probes against a stable model image and assert p95 within golden thresholds
Regression test: inject synthetic 12% TPS degradation in a controlled kernel branch and verify bisector finds the offending commit
Stability run: nightly long-run to measure variance and update baseline automatically if drift is non-customer-impacting
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): run harness against ci-staging runtime and collect baselines (week 1)
Phase 2 (CI gating): enable tps-cohort-prober on PRs affecting runtime and model-kernels with opt-in flag (week 2)
Phase 3 (automatic alerts): wire bisector outputs to PagerDuty + Slack channel with recommended rollback commit link (week 3)
Phase 4 (public dashboards): expose cohort trends to Console per-customer with opt-out for privacy-sensitive setups (post-release)
risks: High variance on short runs can cause false positives; mitigated by adaptive run-length and early-termination heuristics
Cold KV cache cases increase p95 variance; require separate cohort and replay path to isolate kernel vs warmup effects
Cost: long nightly baseline runs consume GPUs; mitigate using preemptible fleet and token caps
Bisector noisy results when multiple commits touch unrelated kernel code; need targeted replay harness that replays requests deterministically
monitoring: Emit per-cohort p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec to metrics namespace tps.cohort.*
Create alert tps.cohort.p95.regression with threshold delta configurable in Console
Log bisector runs with tags: {commit_range, suspected_commit, cohort, quant_profile}
